digest.component_or_area: reconciler bridge_state cache and tickets repository storage
propositions: The reconciler's .bridge_state cache comprises 92% of the 1.04 GiB tickets branch; bookkeeping fields baseline_advanced_at and last_get_pass are written frequently but read nowhere, causing scattered edits that defeat git delta compression and create 12.79 KB marginal cost per bindings.json version.

Eliminating the timestamp field and moving rotation bookkeeping to a separate file reduces marginal pack cost to 1.74 KB per version (7.4x improvement), and version count halves once rotation tracking moves out (12.8x total).

A one-time history rewrite using git fast-export/fast-import with content filtering can reduce the tickets branch from 1.17 GB to 98.8 MB (8.4%) while preserving all commits, merges, and producing a byte-identical HEAD tree when the current state is dynamically re-added.

The rollout requires three format changes to bindings.json: A1 removes baseline_advanced_at, A2 moves last_get_pass to get_rotation.json with backward-compatible max(new,legacy) reads, and A4 narrows prev_snapshot.json to key-set while recording forward/reverse corpus diffs; all are reversible via mixed-version read seams.

Store-epoch guards at union and push sites enforce fail-closed behavior on stale clones before and after history rewrite, with quiesced writer pause and explicit runtime refresh proving epoch mismatch refusal before reclaim publication.

Post-publish rollback uses an off-repo verified bundle and operator-controlled ref reset with forced writer reclone to restore the unfiltered history, preserving fail-closed epoch behavior rather than relying on application-level union logic.
